title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
statement: You are given a list of non-negative integers heights, where heights[i] is the height of the i-th bar of a histogram and every bar has width 1. Return the area of the largest axis-aligned rectangle that fits entirely within the histogram. A rectangle spanning bars from index l to index r (inclusive) is valid only if its height does not exceed any bar in that span, so its area is (r - l + 1) times the minimum bar height over that span. Return a single integer: the maximum such area over all spans. If heights is empty, return 0.
reference_solution:
def largest_rectangle_area(heights):
    stack = []
    best = 0
    extended = list(heights) + [0]
    for i, h in enumerate(extended):
        while stack and extended[stack[-1]] > h:
            top = stack.pop()
            left = stack[-1] if stack else -1
            width = i - left - 1
            best = max(best, extended[top] * width)
        stack.append(i)
    return best
hints: For each bar, the widest rectangle capped at that bar's height extends left and right until it hits a strictly shorter bar. How can you find those boundaries without re-scanning for every bar?
Keep a stack of bar indices whose heights are increasing. When a new bar is shorter than the stack's top, that top bar's right boundary is found, so pop it and settle its rectangle now.

When you pop index top for an incoming bar at index i, the left boundary is the new stack top (or -1 if the stack is empty), so the width is i - left - 1, not i - top. Append a sentinel bar of height 0 at the end so every remaining bar on the stack gets flushed and measured.
